questions.question: Which part of speech names a person, place, thing, or idea?
questions.explanation: A noun names a person, place, thing, or idea.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nouns name things.

questions.question: Which part of speech shows action or being?
questions.explanation: A verb shows action or a state of being.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Verbs show action.

questions.question: Which part of speech describes a noun?
questions.explanation: An adjective describes or modifies a noun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adjectives describe nouns.

questions.question: Which part of speech describes a verb, adjective, or adverb?
questions.explanation: An adverb modifies verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Adverbs describe actions.

questions.question: Which part of speech takes the place of a noun?
questions.explanation: A pronoun replaces a noun, like he, she, or they.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pronouns stand in for nouns.

questions.question: Which part of speech shows the relationship between a noun and another word?
questions.explanation: A preposition like in, on, or under shows a relationship.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Prepositions show relationships.

questions.question: Which part of speech joins words or groups of words?
questions.explanation: A conjunction like and, but, or or joins words or clauses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Conjunctions join things.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The dog ran quickly,' what part of speech is 'quickly'?
questions.explanation: Quickly describes how the dog ran, so it is an adverb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Quickly describes the action.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The happy child laughed,' what part of speech is 'happy'?
questions.explanation: Happy describes the noun child, so it is an adjective.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Happy describes the child.

questions.question: In the sentence 'She and I went home,' what part of speech is 'and'?
questions.explanation: And joins she and I, so it is a conjunction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: And joins the words.

questions.question: What is the subject of the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat'?
questions.explanation: The subject is who or what the sentence is about: the cat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The subject does the action.

questions.question: What is the predicate of the sentence 'The cat sat on the mat'?
questions.explanation: The predicate tells what the subject did: sat on the mat.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The predicate tells what happened.

questions.question: What is a complete sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: A group of words with a subject and a predicate that expresses a complete thought
distractors: A group of words with only a subject
A group of words that ends in a question mark only
questions.explanation: A complete sentence needs a subject, a verb, and a complete thought.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Complete sentences need subject plus verb.

questions.question: Which of these is a sentence fragment?
distractors: The dog ran down the street.
questions.explanation: Running down the street has no subject and no complete thought, so it is a fragment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fragments are missing a piece.

questions.question: Which of these is a run-on sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: I went to the store I bought milk.
distractors: I went to the store, and I bought milk.
I went to the store. I bought milk.
I went to the store because I needed milk.
questions.explanation: Two sentences joined without punctuation or a conjunction is a run-on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Run-ons jam sentences together.

questions.question: What is a simple sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: A sentence with one independent clause
distractors: A sentence with two independent clauses
A sentence with a dependent clause
questions.explanation: A simple sentence has one subject and one predicate, one clause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Simple means one clause.

questions.question: What is a compound sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: A sentence with two independent clauses joined by a conjunction or semicolon
distractors: A sentence with a dependent clause only
questions.explanation: A compound sentence joins two complete thoughts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Compound means two complete thoughts.

questions.question: What is a complex sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: A sentence with one independent clause and at least one dependent clause
distractors: A sentence with two independent clauses
questions.explanation: A complex sentence mixes a main clause with a dependent clause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Complex mixes main and dependent.

questions.question: What is a compound-complex sentence?
questions.correctAnswer: A sentence with two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause
distractors: A sentence with two dependent clauses only
questions.explanation: A compound-complex sentence has at least two main clauses plus a dependent clause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Compound-complex has it all.

questions.question: What is an independent clause?
questions.correctAnswer: A clause that can stand alone as a sentence
distractors: A clause that cannot stand alone
A group of words that is a fragment
questions.explanation: An independent clause has a subject and verb and expresses a complete thought.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Independent clauses stand alone.

questions.question: What is a dependent clause?
questions.correctAnswer: A clause that cannot stand alone as a sentence
distractors: A clause that can stand alone
questions.explanation: A dependent clause starts with a subordinating word and needs a main clause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dependent clauses need help.

questions.question: Which word starts a dependent clause in 'Because it rained, we stayed home'?
questions.explanation: Because is a subordinating conjunction that starts the dependent clause.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Because starts the dependent part.

questions.question: What is a phrase?
questions.correctAnswer: A group of words without a subject and a verb
distractors: A group with a subject and verb
questions.explanation: A phrase lacks either a subject or a verb, or both.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Phrases are missing a subject or verb.

questions.question: What is a prepositional phrase?
questions.correctAnswer: A phrase that begins with a preposition and ends with a noun or pronoun
distractors: A phrase that begins with a verb
A phrase that is a complete sentence
A phrase with a subject and verb
questions.explanation: A prepositional phrase starts with a word like in, on, or under.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Prepositional phrases start with prepositions.

questions.question: In the sentence 'The book on the table is mine,' what is the prepositional phrase?
questions.explanation: On the table starts with the preposition on.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: On the table is the prepositional phrase.

questions.question: What is an appositive?
questions.correctAnswer: A noun or noun phrase that renames another noun
distractors: A clause that starts a sentence
questions.explanation: An appositive renames a nearby noun, like 'my friend, Maya.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Appositives rename nouns.

questions.question: In the sentence 'My sister, a doctor, lives in Phoenix,' what is the appositive?
questions.explanation: A doctor renames my sister.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A doctor renames my sister.

questions.question: What is a participle?
questions.correctAnswer: A verb form used as an adjective, like 'running' or 'broken'
distractors: A verb used as a noun
A noun used as a verb
questions.explanation: Participles are verb forms that describe nouns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Participles describe like adjectives.

questions.question: What is a gerund?
questions.correctAnswer: A verb form ending in -ing used as a noun
distractors: A verb form used as an adjective
A noun used as a verb
questions.explanation: A gerund acts as a noun, like 'Swimming is fun.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gerunds are -ing nouns.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Swimming is fun,' what is 'swimming'?
questions.explanation: Swimming is the subject, so the -ing form acts as a noun.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Swimming is the subject noun.

questions.question: What is an infinitive?
questions.correctAnswer: The base form of a verb with 'to,' like 'to run'
distractors: A verb in the past tense
questions.explanation: An infinitive is 'to' plus the verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Infinitives start with to.

questions.question: In the sentence 'I like to read,' what is 'to read'?
questions.explanation: To read is 'to' plus the base verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: To read is an infinitive.

questions.question: What is active voice?
distractors: The verb is in the past tense
questions.explanation: In active voice, the subject does the action: 'The dog chased the cat.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Active means the subject acts.

questions.question: What is passive voice?
distractors: The verb is in the future tense
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the subject is acted on: 'The cat was chased by the dog.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Passive means the subject is acted on.

questions.question: Which sentence is in active voice?
distractors: The letter was written by Maria.
questions.explanation: Maria performs the action, so it is active.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Maria wrote it, so it is active.

questions.question: Which sentence is in passive voice?
questions.correctAnswer: The cake was baked by Ana.
questions.explanation: The cake receives the action, so it is passive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The cake was baked, so it is passive.

questions.question: What is the indicative mood?
questions.correctAnswer: The mood used for facts and statements
distractors: The mood used for questions only
questions.explanation: Indicative mood states facts: 'She is here.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Indicative states facts.

questions.question: What is the imperative mood?
questions.correctAnswer: The mood used for commands and requests
questions.explanation: Imperative mood gives commands: 'Close the door.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Imperative gives commands.

questions.question: What is the subjunctive mood?
questions.correctAnswer: The mood used for wishes, suggestions, or hypothetical situations
questions.explanation: Subjunctive mood expresses wishes: 'I wish I were taller.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Subjunctive is for wishes.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood?
questions.explanation: I wish I were expresses a wish, using the subjunctive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wish sentences use subjunctive.

questions.question: What is verb tense?
questions.correctAnswer: The form of a verb that shows when an action happens
questions.explanation: Tense shows past, present, or future time.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tense shows time.

questions.question: What is the past tense of 'go'?
questions.explanation: The past tense of go is went.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Went is the past of go.

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'eat'?
questions.explanation: The past participle of eat is eaten.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Eaten is the past participle.

questions.question: What is the present perfect tense of 'I walk'?
questions.explanation: Present perfect uses have plus the past participle.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Have walked is present perfect.

questions.question: What is the future tense of 'she runs'?
questions.explanation: Future tense uses will plus the base verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Will run is future.

questions.question: What is subject-verb agreement?
questions.correctAnswer: The verb must match the subject in number
distractors: The verb must match the object
The subject must match the adjective
The verb must be in the past tense
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Subjects and verbs must agree.

questions.question: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement?
distractors: The dog barks loudly and the dogs barks.
questions.explanation: Dogs is plural, so the verb bark is correct.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plural subject, plural verb.

questions.question: What is a pronoun's antecedent?
questions.explanation: The antecedent is the noun the pronoun stands for.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The antecedent is the noun replaced.

questions.question: In the sentence 'Ana lost her book,' what is the antecedent of 'her'?
questions.explanation: Her refers back to Ana.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Her points to Ana.

questions.question: Which pronoun is correct: '___ and I went to the store'?
questions.explanation: He is a subject pronoun, so it fits as the subject.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: He is the subject form.

questions.question: Which pronoun is correct: 'The teacher gave the book to ___'?
questions.explanation: Me is an object pronoun, so it fits after the preposition to.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Me is the object form.

questions.question: What is an intensive pronoun?
questions.correctAnswer: A pronoun that emphasizes a noun, like 'myself' in 'I did it myself'
distractors: A pronoun that replaces a noun
A pronoun that asks a question
questions.explanation: Intensive pronouns add emphasis and can be removed without changing the meaning.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Myself adds emphasis.

questions.question: What is a reflexive pronoun?
questions.correctAnswer: A pronoun that refers back to the subject, like 'herself'
distractors: A pronoun that replaces a noun
A pronoun that asks a question
questions.explanation: Reflexive pronouns are needed when the subject and object are the same.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Reflexive points back to the subject.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a reflexive pronoun correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: She taught herself to play piano.
distractors: She taught himself to play piano.
She taught themselves to play piano.
She taught itself to play piano.
questions.explanation: Herself matches the subject she.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Herself matches she.

questions.question: When do you use a comma after an introductory phrase?
questions.correctAnswer: After a phrase that starts a sentence, before the main clause
questions.explanation: Use a comma after an introductory element, like 'After dinner, we went home.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Intro phrases get a comma.

questions.question: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: After dinner, we went for a walk.
distractors: After dinner we went for a walk.
After, dinner we went for a walk.
After dinner, we, went for a walk.
questions.explanation: A comma follows the introductory phrase after dinner.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Intro comma after dinner.

questions.question: When do you use a semicolon?
questions.correctAnswer: To join two closely related independent clauses
distractors: To join a dependent clause only
To replace a comma in a list of two items
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two complete thoughts without a conjunction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Semicolons join complete thoughts.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: I love reading; my sister loves movies.
distractors: I love reading; because it is fun.
I love reading; and my sister loves movies.
questions.explanation: Both sides of the semicolon are complete sentences.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Both sides are complete.

questions.question: When do you use a colon?
questions.correctAnswer: To introduce a list, an explanation, or a quotation
questions.explanation: A colon comes before a list or explanation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Colons introduce lists.

questions.question: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: Bring these items: a notebook, a pen, and a ruler.
distractors: Bring these items, a notebook: a pen.
Bring these items a notebook, a pen, and: a ruler.
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the list.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The colon starts the list.

questions.question: When do you use an apostrophe?
questions.correctAnswer: To show possession or a contraction
questions.explanation: Apostrophes show ownership or missing letters in contractions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Apostrophes show possession or contractions.

questions.question: Which word is the correct possessive form of 'dog'?
questions.explanation: Add an apostrophe and s for a singular possessive.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dog's shows one dog owns it.

questions.question: Which sentence uses quotation marks correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: She said, 'I will be there soon.'
distractors: She said, I will be there soon.
She said 'I will be there soon'.
She said, I will be there soon.'
questions.explanation: Quotation marks go around the exact words spoken.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Quotes go around spoken words.

questions.question: What is parallel structure?
questions.correctAnswer: Using the same grammatical form for items in a list
distractors: Using different forms in a list
questions.explanation: Parallel structure keeps list items in the same form.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Parallel lists match in form.

questions.question: Which sentence has parallel structure?
questions.correctAnswer: She likes reading, writing, and swimming.
distractors: She likes reading, to write, and swimming.
She likes to read, writing, and swim.
She likes reading, writing, and to swim.
questions.explanation: All three items are gerunds, so they are parallel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: All three are -ing forms.

questions.question: What is a dangling modifier?
questions.correctAnswer: A phrase that does not clearly modify the word it should
distractors: A phrase that is too long
A clause that is too short
questions.explanation: A dangling modifier is misplaced, like 'Running late, the bus left without me.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dangling modifiers point at the wrong word.

questions.question: Which sentence has a dangling modifier?
questions.correctAnswer: Running late, the bus left without me.
distractors: Running late, I missed the bus.
I missed the bus because I was running late.
questions.explanation: Running late should describe I, not the bus.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The bus was not running late.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'their,' 'there,' and 'they're'?
questions.correctAnswer: Their shows possession, there shows place, they're means they are
distractors: Their shows place, there shows possession
questions.explanation: Their is possessive, there is a place, and they're is a contraction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Their, there, they're are different.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'your' and 'you're'?
questions.correctAnswer: Your shows possession; you're means you are
distractors: Your means you are; you're shows possession
questions.explanation: Your is possessive and you're is a contraction of you are.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Your owns, you're means you are.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'its' and 'it's'?
questions.correctAnswer: Its shows possession; it's means it is
distractors: Its means it is; it's shows possession
questions.explanation: Its is possessive and it's is a contraction.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Its owns, it's means it is.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'to,' 'too,' and 'two'?
questions.correctAnswer: To is a preposition, too means also or very, two is the number 2
distractors: To is the number, too is a preposition
questions.explanation: To, too, and two sound alike but have different meanings.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: To, too, two are different.

questions.question: What is a simile?
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison using like or as
distractors: A comparison without like or as
questions.explanation: A simile compares with like or as: 'brave as a lion.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Similes use like or as.

questions.question: What is a metaphor?
questions.correctAnswer: A comparison without using like or as
distractors: A comparison using like or as
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing is another: 'Time is money.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Metaphors say it is.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a simile?
questions.correctAnswer: Her smile was as bright as the sun.
questions.explanation: As bright as the sun uses as to compare.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: As bright as the sun is a simile.

questions.question: Which sentence contains a metaphor?
distractors: The classroom was like a zoo.
The classroom was as noisy as a zoo.
questions.explanation: The classroom was a zoo compares without like or as.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: A zoo is a metaphor.

questions.question: What is personification?
questions.correctAnswer: Giving human qualities to nonhuman things
questions.explanation: Personification gives human traits to objects, like 'The wind whispered.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Personification makes things human.

questions.question: What is hyperbole?
distractors: A word that imitates a sound
questions.explanation: Hyperbole exaggerates, like 'I have told you a million times.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hyperbole is a big exaggeration.

questions.question: What is onomatopoeia?
questions.correctAnswer: A word that imitates a sound, like 'buzz' or 'crash'
questions.explanation: Onomatopoeia words sound like what they describe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Buzz sounds like buzzing.

questions.question: What is the correct spelling: 'separate' or 'seperate'?
questions.explanation: Separate is spelled s-e-p-a-r-a-t-e.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Separate has par in the middle.

questions.question: What is the correct spelling: 'necessary' or 'neccessary'?
questions.explanation: Necessary has one c and two s letters.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Necessary has one c and two s.

questions.question: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: Definitely is spelled d-e-f-i-n-i-t-e-l-y.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Definitely ends in -itely.

questions.question: What does the prefix 'un-' mean?
questions.explanation: Un- means not, as in unhappy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Un- means not.

questions.question: What does the prefix 're-' mean?
questions.explanation: Re- means again, as in redo.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Re- means again.

questions.question: What does the prefix 'pre-' mean?
questions.explanation: Pre- means before, as in preview.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pre- means before.

questions.question: What does the suffix '-ful' mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of, as in helpful.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -ful means full of.

questions.question: What does the suffix '-less' mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -less means without, as in hopeless.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -less means without.

questions.question: What does the suffix '-able' mean?
questions.explanation: The suffix -able means able to be, as in readable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: -able means able to be.

questions.question: What is the root 'dict' from Latin?
questions.explanation: Dict means to say, as in dictate and predict.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dict means to say.

questions.question: What is the root 'graph' from Greek?
questions.explanation: Graph means to write, as in autograph.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Graph means to write.

questions.question: What is the root 'port' from Latin?
questions.explanation: Port means to carry, as in transport and portable.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Port means to carry.

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'happy'?
questions.explanation: Joyful means the same as happy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Joyful is like happy.

questions.question: Which word is an antonym for 'brave'?
questions.explanation: Cowardly is the opposite of brave.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cowardly is the opposite of brave.

questions.question: What is the tone of a piece of writing?
questions.correctAnswer: The writer's attitude toward the subject
questions.explanation: Tone is the attitude the writer shows through word choice.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tone is the writer's attitude.

questions.question: What is the main idea of a paragraph?
questions.correctAnswer: The most important point the paragraph makes
questions.explanation: The main idea is the central point, supported by details.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: The main idea is the central point.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'good'?
questions.explanation: The comparative of good is better; the superlative is best.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Better compares two.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of 'good'?
questions.explanation: The superlative of good is best.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Best is the most.

questions.question: What is the comparative form of 'bad'?
questions.explanation: The comparative of bad is worse; the superlative is worst.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Worse compares two.

questions.question: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.correctAnswer: I bought apples, oranges, and bananas.
distractors: I bought apples oranges and bananas.
I bought apples, oranges and, bananas.
I bought, apples oranges and bananas.
questions.explanation: Use commas to separate items in a list, with a comma before and.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Commas separate list items.

questions.question: What is a homophone?
questions.correctAnswer: A word that sounds the same as another but has a different meaning
distractors: A word with the same meaning
A word with the opposite meaning
A word with the same spelling
questions.explanation: Homophones like to, too, and two sound alike but differ.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Homophones sound alike.

questions.question: What is the main idea of a story's theme?
questions.correctAnswer: The lesson or message the story teaches
questions.explanation: Theme is the central message or lesson.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Theme is the lesson.
